Subject: Nexus RFP — SLO measurement & evidence acceptance questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick responses so far. The procurement and SRE teams at Nexus have one final block of clarifying questions on your proposed SLOs in the RFP. Before we move to formal contract language we need a short, actionable acceptance checklist that we can hand to our legal and compliance teams. Key items we need:

- Precise event definition for "unavailable" (what endpoints, status codes, throttled vs queued requests)
- Measurement windowing and how partial-minute outages are attributed
- Sampling strategy (synthetic probes vs production sampling) and minimum sample sizes per region
- How multi-region routing and weighted windows affect the uptime calculation
- Service credit calculation trigger and remediation timeline

Can you share a short playbook (3–6 pages) or checklist and an example evidence bundle (SLA annex + sample telemetry) that we can attach to the SOW? Also please include a contact we can escalate to if there is disagreement over attribution.

Appreciate it — we aim to finalize procurement by end of next week.

Best,

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are two artifacts we typically provide in RFP responses: 1) SLA_Annex_v1.pdf (contract-ready annex with definitions and credit matrix) and 2) SLA_Measurement_Playbook.odt (operational checklist + example evidence bundle). Highlights below (short form):

1) Unavailable definition
- "Unavailable" = server error (5xx) OR request timeout as observed at the platform ingress for the public inference endpoint(s) we expose (text-generation/api/v1/generate). Client-side retries that reach the service are considered separate successful/failed attempts.

2) Attribution & windowing
- Primary measurement window: rolling 1-minute buckets aggregated to 1h and 30d windows for crediting.
- Partial-minute incidents: we use second-level telemetry to prorate the minute where applicable; incidents shorter than 5s are recorded but excluded from credit calculation unless they aggregate across >=3 disjoint minutes within a 1h window.

3) Sampling strategy
- Production telemetry: 100% of ingress success/failure counters recorded with 1s resolution for customer-specific routes under Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers receive aggregated counters at 1s resolution with 10s export.
- Synthetic probes: optional; for multi-region customers we recommend 1 probe/min/region and a 5m rolling median to catch routing-based failures. Minimum sample requirement for regional SLA validity: 1k probes/day or 10k requests sampling/day (either production or synthetic).

4) Multi-region weighting
- By default, availability is computed per-region and weighted by observed request volume for the contract period. Customers can request fixed-region weighting in the annex.

5) Service credits
- Credit trigger: sustained availability breach of the monthly SLO (e.g., availability < 99.9% for the month) after accounting for exclusions (maintenance windows, customer-side misconfig).
- Remediation timeline: initial investigation within 24h, provisional credit estimate within 5 business days, final adjudication within 20 business days.

Next steps: if Nexus is comfortable with the annex, we'll provide an evidence template (CSV + query snippets from our telemetry backend) and a short adjudication workflow that names a technical contact (we propose Karthik Iyer — karthik.iyer@redwood.ai) for any disputes.

I attached the annex and playbook. If useful I can convert the playbook into a 1‑page checklist for procurement.

Thanks,

Aisha — quick operational clarifications from the runtime side (sorry for the micro-details, but these come up in adjudication):

- "Queued" vs "throttled": our runtime emits distinct event types. Throttles that are returned to clients (429 responses) are counted as failed requests for availability unless "graceful backoff" is configured in the customer routing policy in the annex.
- Clock sync: we timestamp all telemetry in UTC with NTP-synced hosts; for multi-region incidents we align windows to the customer-configured time zone at contract inception.
- Edge burst windows: we treat bursts > 3x baseline rate that cause transient internal queue overflows as mitigatable if they match a documented traffic spike pattern; otherwise they are counted against availability. We capture 1s-resolution histograms to demonstrate burst attribution.

I'll include the sample PromQL/Flux snippets and a small anonymized evidence CSV when Vanessa confirms and we'll drop it into the Drive link Vanessa already referenced.
